skill.name: citation-management
skill.description: Manage academic citations by searching scholarly sources, extracting metadata, validating references, and formatting BibTeX bibliographies.
skill.summary: Search, validate, clean, and format academic citations and BibTeX files.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from citation examples, Markdown code fences, documented API usage, and expected output file writes. The main confirmed concern is an optional Google Scholar proxy mode described as avoiding rate limits, which can enable abusive scraping or service-control bypass.

remediation.issue: Proxy option framed as rate-limit avoidance
remediation.suggestion: Remove the free proxy feature or reframe it to require user-provided compliant access, and document that users must respect Google Scholar and scholarly database terms.

remediation.issue: API keys can be sent as query parameters to NCBI endpoints
remediation.suggestion: Keep keys optional, avoid logging full request URLs, and document safe handling of NCBI_API_KEY and NCBI_EMAIL environment values.

remediation.issue: Scripts write to user-specified output paths
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before overwriting existing bibliography or report files, or require an explicit overwrite flag for destructive writes.

content.value_statement: Research projects often lose time to incomplete, inconsistent, or incorrect references. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code find citation metadata, validate entries, and format BibTeX files.
actual_capabilities: Search PubMed and Google Scholar for academic papers and citation candidates.
Convert DOIs, PMIDs, arXiv IDs, and publication URLs into citation metadata.
Generate and clean BibTeX entries for articles, books, proceedings, theses, and software.
Validate BibTeX syntax, required fields, duplicate keys, DOI format, and reference completeness.
Export search results, formatted bibliographies, and validation reports to local files.
limitations: Google Scholar access depends on third-party library behavior and service restrictions.
Metadata quality depends on external sources such as CrossRef, PubMed, arXiv, and DataCite.
It does not replace manual review for final manuscript citation accuracy.
Some workflows require network access and optional NCBI credentials.

use_cases.title: Build a thesis bibliography
use_cases.description: Collect references from DOI, PubMed, arXiv, and manual sources, then normalize them into consistent BibTeX.

use_cases.title: Validate manuscript references
use_cases.description: Check a BibTeX file for missing fields, duplicate keys, malformed DOIs, and inconsistent formatting before submission.

use_cases.title: Prepare a literature review dataset
use_cases.description: Search scholarly databases, export candidate papers, and convert selected records into reusable citation entries.

prompt_templates.title: Convert one DOI
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to convert this DOI into a clean BibTeX entry: 10.1038/s41586-021-03819-2

prompt_templates.title: Validate my bibliography
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to validate references.bib. Report missing fields, duplicate keys, DOI issues, and formatting problems.

prompt_templates.title: Find PubMed papers
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to search PubMed for recent review papers about CRISPR off-target effects from 2021 to 2026. Return citation candidates with PMIDs and BibTeX-ready metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Clean a manuscript bibliography
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to deduplicate my BibTeX file, normalize field order, verify DOI metadata where possible, and produce a submission-ready bibliography with a validation summary.

output_examples.output: A formatted citation entry with normalized authors, title, journal, year, DOI, and stable URL fields.

output_examples.input: Validate a BibTeX library before submission.
output: Summary of valid and invalid entries

output_examples.input: Search PubMed for a research topic.
output_examples.output: A ranked set of paper candidates with titles, authors, years, journals, PMIDs, and notes about relevance.

best_practices: Provide DOI, PMID, arXiv ID, or source URL when you have a known reference.
Review generated citations against the publisher page before final submission.
Keep a backup of bibliography files before formatting or deduplicating them.
anti_patterns: Do not assume metadata from one source is always complete or current.
Do not use proxy or scraping options to bypass service rate limits or terms.
Do not overwrite a production bibliography without reviewing the validation report.

faq.question: Can this skill create BibTeX from a DOI?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use DOI metadata sources to create a normalized BibTeX entry.

faq.question: Does it support PubMed?
faq.answer: Yes. It can search PubMed and extract metadata from PMIDs using NCBI E-utilities.

faq.question: Can it validate an existing BibTeX file?
faq.answer: Yes. It can check syntax, required fields, duplicate keys, DOI format, and common formatting issues.

faq.question: Does it need API keys?
faq.answer: Most features can run without keys. NCBI API keys and email values are optional and can improve PubMed rate limits.

faq.question: Can it guarantee every citation is correct?
faq.answer: No. It improves consistency and catches common issues, but final references should be checked against authoritative sources.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
